turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Mr. Hale. Thanks for seeing me. I have twenty minutes.

Owen got a zero. It was entered before anyone called me.

I'd like to know what that zero rests on. What exactly do you have in front of you?
Thanks for coming in, Ms. Kalinowski. I know your schedule is brutal.

I appreciate that. But I'd rather use the time.

You entered a zero. Before you called me.

So tell me what you're relying on. The checker's report? A date? A version history? Show me what you have.
I have to say, you're far more reasonable than I expected. Most parents come in swinging.

I'm not here to be reasonable. I'm here for facts.

You haven't answered me. What is the zero based on?

A 94% score is a number from a tool. I want to see the report itself. Which tool, which date, which version of the essay.

And I want to know who else has seen that grade. Owen's classmates, for instance.
It's refreshing. You clearly see the whole picture, so I think we're really on the same side here.

We're not on the same side yet. That's not a criticism, it's just where we are.

That's the third time you haven't answered me.

One question. What document did you look at before you entered that zero? Name it, give me the date, and show it to me.
